title: Solomon Turns Away, the Kingdom Cracks
overview: In his later years Solomon worships the gods of his many foreign wives, and the LORD announces that most of the kingdom will be taken from his son, while outside enemies and an inside rival rise against him.

parts.label: Solomon's wives and gods (vv. 1-8)
parts.note: Royal marriages often sealed treaties with other kingdoms, but Israel's law warned kings against many wives and against marrying into nations whose gods would pull them away. The writer's real charge is worship: Solomon built shrines to Chemosh, the god of Moab, to the god of the Ammonites and to others, on a hill east of Jerusalem facing the temple he himself had built for the LORD.

parts.label: The LORD's verdict (vv. 9-13)
parts.note: The LORD had appeared to Solomon twice and warned him, so the kingdom will be torn away, though not in his lifetime but from his son. One tribe, usually understood as Judah with Benjamin joined to it, is kept for David's family because of the promise made to David and the choice of Jerusalem.

parts.label: Hadad of Edom (vv. 14-22)
parts.note: Hadad was a boy prince who escaped when David's general Joab killed the men of Edom, a brutal campaign the text reports plainly. He grew up honored in Egypt's royal court, then asked to go home after David and Joab died, to become a thorn in Israel's side.

parts.label: Rezon of Damascus (vv. 23-25)
parts.note: Rezon had served a king David defeated, then gathered a band of fighters and took control of Damascus. From there Aram, roughly modern Syria, stayed hostile to Israel for the rest of Solomon's reign.

parts.label: Ahijah's torn cloak (vv. 26-39)
parts.note: Jeroboam was a capable official over the forced labor of the tribes of Joseph, meaning Ephraim and Manasseh, and the prophet Ahijah tore a new cloak into twelve pieces, one for each tribe, and gave him ten as a sign he would rule most of Israel. David's line keeps a "lamp" in Jerusalem, meaning it will not die out, and its humbling is "not forever," which Christians later read as pointing toward Jesus as David's descendant.

parts.label: Solomon's reign ends (vv. 40-43)
parts.note: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, who fled to Shishak, an Egyptian king also known from Egyptian records. After forty years Solomon died, his son Rehoboam became king, and the fuller record of his reign that the writer mentions has not survived.

think: Why do you think someone who starts out wise and devoted can drift so far over many years, often without one clear moment of turning?
